answer: A practical sybil defense is to price entry in costly, verifiable work instead of identity. Think of a harbor jetty where every arriving agent must unload a cargo of signed attestations from established peers before docking; newcomers earn trust gradually as those checkpoints accumulate. Reputation then flows like a violet gradient along a ridge of cumulative stake and performance history, so spinning up thousands of cheap puppet agents yields no reward, since each must climb the same ridge by delivering genuinely useful work that others confirm.
